members.working:
Identify product containing named element in each reaction under given conditions.
(i) Ni²⁺ + NH₄OH + H₂S → NiS (precipitate). NiS is typically antiferromagnetic? NiS (hexagonal) is paramagnetic? Usually NiS (wurtzite) is paramagnetic due to unpaired d electrons. So paramagnetic.
(ii) FeCl₃ + H₂ (heating) → Fe (metal) or FeCl₂? Reaction reduces Fe(III) to Fe(0) or Fe metal? Likely Fe metal formed, which is paramagnetic (Fe metal has unpaired electrons). So paramagnetic.
(iii) NH₃ + O₂, burning, pale yellow flame → N₂O? Actually combustion of NH₃ gives N₂ + H₂O? Pale yellow flame suggests combustion of organic? But product containing N likely N₂ (non-paramagnetic). N₂ is diamagnetic. So not paramagnetic.
(iv) KMnO₄ + H₂O₂ + H₂SO₄ → MnO₂ (common reduction product). MnO₂ contains Mn(IV) with d⁵? MnO₂ is antiferromagnetic? Typically MnO₂ is paramagnetic (high spin d⁵). So paramagnetic.
(v) CoCl₂ + NH₄Cl + excess NH₃ + air bubbled through + charcoal → Co(OH)₃ or CoO? Likely Co(OH)₃ or CoO, paramagnetic (Co(III) d⁶ low spin? Could be antiferromagnetic? Usually Co(III) compounds are low spin and diamagnetic? But Co(II) complexes are paramagnetic. The product likely Co(OH)₂ or Co(OH)₃; Co(III) often low spin d⁶ (t2g⁶) diamagnetic. However typical reaction of CoCl₂ with NH₃ gives Co(NH₃)₆²⁺ paramagnetic. With air and charcoal may oxidize to Co₃O₄? Co₃O₄ is antiferromagnetic? Likely paramagnetic. Assume paramagnetic.
(vi) FeCl₂ + O₂ heating in air → FeO or Fe₃O₄? FeO (II) paramagnetic? FeO (rock salt) is antiferromagnetic? Fe₃O₄ (magnetite) is ferrimagnetic (paramagnetic at high T). Likely paramagnetic.
(vii) Na₂Cr₂O₇ + KCl fractional crystallisation → CrCl₃ or Cr₂O₃? Cr(III) compounds are low spin d³, paramagnetic (three unpaired). So paramagnetic.
Thus reactions (i),(ii),(iv),(v),(vi),(vii) paramagnetic =6; (iii) not. So answer 6.
